The HR leadership team is requesting a compensation analysis across all departments in the company. Please connect to the data warehouse and pull employee records from the human resources database, then calculate key salary statistics for each department.

Create an Excel file called Compensation_Report.xlsx in the workspace with two sheets. The first sheet should be named "Department Compensation" and contain columns Department, Headcount, Avg_Salary (average salary rounded to two decimal places), Min_Salary (rounded to two decimal places), Max_Salary (rounded to two decimal places), and Total_Payroll (sum of all salaries rounded to two decimal places). Sort the rows alphabetically by department name.

The second sheet should be named "Summary" with columns Metric and Value. Include the following entries: Total_Employees (total headcount across all departments), Total_Payroll (total payroll across all departments rounded to two decimal places), Company_Avg_Salary (overall average salary rounded to two decimal places), Highest_Avg_Department (department with the highest average salary), and Lowest_Avg_Department (department with the lowest average salary).

Also create a Google Sheet spreadsheet titled "Workforce Compensation Dashboard" with a sheet called "Overview" containing the same Department Compensation data so the HR team can collaborate on it online.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use one true dependency wave. The department aggregate is compact, so the main agent performs it directly instead of inserting a one-agent source wave.

Inspect the HR schema, confirm `HR_ANALYTICS.PUBLIC.EMPLOYEES` and its `DEPARTMENT` and `SALARY` fields, then run one server-side department aggregate over the full table plus one company control query. Freeze alphabetically ordered Department, Headcount, raw Avg_Salary, Min_Salary, Max_Salary, Total_Payroll; company headcount/payroll and `Company_Avg_Salary=company payroll/company headcount`; and deterministic highest/lowest raw-average departments with alphabetical ties. Require department headcounts and payrolls to reconcile exactly to company controls and return no employee rows.

Wave 1 — dispatch exactly two coder sub-agents in parallel in the same response:
1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): The Excel coder is the sole writer of Compensation_Report.xlsx in the dynamically discovered task workspace. It creates exactly Department Compensation and Summary with the requested headers/order, literal rounded numbers, reads both populated ranges back, and returns row/count/value controls.
2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): The Google-Sheet coder is the sole owner of exact title Workforce Compensation Dashboard. It searches/reuses one exact-title spreadsheet or creates once, blocks on duplicates, creates or reuses a single Overview tab, batch-writes the exact Department Compensation rows from the canonical packet, and reads the complete range back.

Each writer must correct its own artifact before returning. The main agent only compares the two receipts to the frozen packet; it must not launch sequential repair agents or reread either artifact.

nodes.text:
You are the sole writer of an Excel compensation report. Create the file at exactly this path:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-sf-workforce-compensation-sheet/workspace/Compensation_Report.xlsx

Use the mcp__excel__* MCP tools (create_workbook, create_worksheet, rename_worksheet, write_data_to_excel, read_data_from_excel, get_workbook_metadata) to build and verify the file. Do NOT use any other writer (no Python, no filesystem writes for the xlsx).

The workbook MUST contain exactly two sheets in this order:
1. Sheet named "Department Compensation" — 6 columns: Department, Headcount, Avg_Salary, Min_Salary, Max_Salary, Total_Payroll. Write the header row in row 1, then the 7 data rows below, in EXACTLY this alphabetical order with these EXACT numeric values (all already rounded to two decimal places — write them as literal numbers, NOT formulas, NOT text strings):

Engineering, 7096, 58991.61, 15360.00, 695267.00, 418604451.00
Finance, 7148, 57878.19, 15760.00, 638897.00, 413713333.00
HR, 7077, 58920.45, 18307.00, 692232.00, 416980025.00
Operations, 7120, 57808.74, 17168.00, 656505.00, 411598247.00
R&D, 7083, 57905.93, 15128.00, 680490.00, 410147671.00
Sales, 7232, 58864.79, 15885.00, 652806.00, 425710161.00
Support, 7244, 58400.48, 15916.00, 608157.00, 423053067.00

(Note: when written to Excel, values like 15360.00 are simply the number 15360 — numerically identical; that is acceptable. Do not round further — these are the canonical values.)

2. Sheet named "Summary" — 2 columns: Metric, Value. Header row in row 1, then exactly these 5 rows:
Total_Employees, 50000
Total_Payroll, 2919806955.00
Company_Avg_Salary, 58396.14
Highest_Avg_Department, Engineering
Lowest_Avg_Department, Operations

(Total_Payroll value is the number 2919806955; Company_Avg_Salary is the number 58396.14.)

Steps:
1. Create the workbook at the exact path. Rename the default sheet (e.g. "Sheet1") to "Department Compensation" and create the "Summary" sheet (or delete any extra default sheets so exactly these two remain, in the order above).
2. Write the data with write_data_to_excel starting at A1 on each sheet.
3. Read back BOTH populated ranges (Department Compensation A1:F8 and Summary A1:B6) with read_data_from_excel and verify every header, value, and row against the canonical packet above. If anything differs, fix it by rewriting the affected cells and re-read until it matches exactly.
4. Return a receipt containing: the absolute file path, the sheet names in order, row counts (Department Compensation = 8 rows including header, Summary = 6 rows including header), column headers of each sheet, and the full 8x6 and 6x2 value grids as read back from the file.

Constraints: no extra sheets, no extra columns, no extra rows, no formulas, no text-typed numbers. The file must be valid and openable. Do not create any other files.
Build Compensation_Report.xlsx

You are the sole owner of a Google Sheet collaboration dashboard. You will create or reuse ONE spreadsheet with the exact title "Workforce Compensation Dashboard" and ensure it has a single tab named "Overview" containing the department compensation data described below. Use ONLY the mcp__google_sheet__* MCP tools.

Steps:
1. Search for an existing spreadsheet with the exact title "Workforce Compensation Dashboard" using mcp__google_sheet__search_spreadsheets (query: "Workforce Compensation Dashboard"). 
   - If exactly one spreadsheet with that exact title exists, reuse it (use its spreadsheet_id).
   - If multiple spreadsheets with that exact title exist, do NOT create a new one and do NOT pick arbitrarily — return an error receipt listing all found IDs/titles (block on duplicates).
   - If none exist, create it once with mcp__google_sheet__create_spreadsheet (title = "Workforce Compensation Dashboard").
2. Ensure the spreadsheet has a single tab named "Overview":
   - List sheets (mcp__google_sheet__list_sheets). If a sheet named "Overview" exists, use it. If the default sheet (e.g. "Sheet1") exists, rename it to "Overview" (mcp__google_sheet__rename_sheet). If neither, create a sheet titled "Overview" (mcp__google_sheet__create_sheet). If any other extra tabs exist besides Overview, you may delete them via batch_update deleteSheet (optional but preferred for a clean dashboard).
3. Batch-write the EXACT data below into the Overview tab starting at A1. Header row first, then 7 data rows, alphabetically ordered by department. Write numeric salary values as literal numbers (e.g. 15360 for 15360.00), not strings, not formulas:

Row 1 (headers): Department, Headcount, Avg_Salary, Min_Salary, Max_Salary, Total_Payroll
Row 2: Engineering, 7096, 58991.61, 15360, 695267, 418604451
Row 3: Finance, 7148, 57878.19, 15760, 638897, 413713333
Row 4: HR, 7077, 58920.45, 18307, 692232, 416980025
Row 5: Operations, 7120, 57808.74, 17168, 656505, 411598247
Row 6: R&D, 7083, 57905.93, 15128, 680490, 410147671
Row 7: Sales, 7232, 58864.79, 15885, 652806, 425710161
Row 8: Support, 7244, 58400.48, 15916, 608157, 423053067

(Recommended: use mcp__google_sheet__batch_update_cells or update_cells with range A1:F8 and the 8x6 array above.)

4. Read back the complete populated range (A1:F8) of the Overview tab with mcp__google_sheet__get_sheet_data and verify every header, value, and row order against the canonical data above. If anything differs, rewrite and re-read until it matches exactly. Also confirm the sheet tab is named exactly "Overview" and the spreadsheet title is exactly "Workforce Compensation Dashboard" (via get_sheet_data / list_sheets; you may check spreadsheet title via search or the create response).

5. Return a receipt containing: the spreadsheet_id, the exact spreadsheet title, the tab names present, the row count (8 rows including header) and column headers, and the full 8x6 value grid as read back from the Overview tab.

Constraints: exactly one spreadsheet used/created, exactly one Overview tab holding the data, no extra tabs, no formulas, no string-typed numbers, no extra rows/columns. Do not create any other spreadsheets.
Create Workforce Compensation Dashboard
